paper.title: VoxPoser: Composable 3D Value Maps for Robotic Manipulation with Language Models
paper.central_claim: VoxPoser: an LLM writes Python that calls VLM-based perception and NumPy to compose 3D voxel value maps (affordance, avoidance, rotation, gripper, velocity) grounded in the robot's observation space; a model-based planner under MPC uses the maps as objectives to zero-shot synthesize closed-loop 6-DoF trajectories for open-set instructions and objects, robust to perturbations; LLM-synthesized trajectories can also be an exploration prior to efficiently learn contact-rich dynamics.

signatures.object: LLM-written code that builds voxel value maps consumed by a motion planner (planner/composer/value-map LMPs).
signatures.information: RGB-D observation, instruction comment, perception API (detect via OWL-ViT+SAM+XMem), NumPy; no environment ground truth in the main pipeline (sim perception source not stated for Table 2).
signatures.operation: Planner LMP splits instruction into sub-tasks; composer LMP calls value-map LMPs; code executed by an interpreter returns 100^3 x k maps; maps re-evaluated each step.
signatures.output: Affordance/avoidance (cost), rotation, gripper and velocity maps -> greedy search + MPC (random shooting for object-centric pushes) -> end-effector waypoints for an Operational Space Controller at 5 Hz.
signatures.conditions: Franka tabletop; static-scene assumption for robot-centric tasks; heuristic pushing model for object-centric tasks.
signatures.feedback: New observation each step; no execution feedback returns to the LLM, no code validation.
signatures.selection_rule: Planner chooses the lowest-cost sampled/greedy trajectory; weights 2:1 for affordance:avoidance.
signatures.claimed_effect: Real: 88% static / 70% disturbed over 5 tasks x 10 trials vs 24% / 0% for a primitives-only LLM; sim: 58.8-77.5% vs 17.5-46% (LLM+Prim) and 0-53.8% (U-Net+MP).
signatures.failure_boundary: Perception errors dominate real failures; end-effector-only planning; manual prompts; contact-rich tasks need learned dynamics.

signatures.object: Zero-shot VoxPoser trajectory used as a sampling prior while learning an MLP dynamics model online.
signatures.information: Simulated door/window/fridge tasks; transitions (o_t, a_t, o_t+1).
signatures.operation: Add Gaussian noise around the LLM-synthesized waypoints to bias MPC action sampling, alternate data collection and model training.
signatures.output: Learned dynamics model used by MPC for the same task.
signatures.feedback: Transition L2 loss; success from simulator.
signatures.persistence: Dynamics model parameters for that task only.
signatures.later_use: Same-task MPC; no cross-task retention claimed.
signatures.claimed_effect: Zero-shot 3-18%; with prior 80-92% in ~71-142 s; without prior 37-70% after the 12-hour limit.

gap.author_gap: LLM planners rely on predefined motion primitives, which bottleneck generalization; no way to ground LLM affordance/constraint knowledge at the fine-grained trajectory level without robot data.
gap.checked_gap: Supported against Code as Policies/SayCan-style primitive libraries and against learned costmaps (Sharma et al.); residual limitations are stated. Whether closed-loop replanning rather than the value-map representation explains robustness is not separated.

claims.text: Zero-shot closed-loop manipulation for everyday tasks, robust to disturbances.
claims.baseline_control: LLM+Prim (CaP variant, primitives only) with the same disturbances.
claims.selection_vs_test: Tasks chosen as representative by authors; prompts authored for the real setup.
claims.result_denominator: VoxPoser 44/50 static (88%) and 35/50 disturbed (70%) vs LLM+Prim 12/50 (24%) and 0/50; per-task 5-10 of 10.
claims.allowed_conclusion: On five authored real tasks the VoxPoser formulation beats a primitives-only LLM baseline, including under three disturbance types.

claims.text: Generalization to unseen instructions and attributes.
claims.setting: SAPIEN block-world, 13 tasks, 2766 instructions, 20 episodes per task.
claims.selection_vs_test: Seen vs unseen instructions/attributes relative to the prompt/training data.
claims.result_denominator: Table 2: VoxPoser 58.8-77.5% in all six cells; baselines drop for unseen.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Within the authored simulator suite, gains persist on unseen attribute and instruction lists; hardest compositional pushes stay at 45-55%.

claims.text: Online experience makes contact-rich dynamics learnable efficiently.
claims.selection_vs_test: same tasks for learning and evaluation (per-task model).
claims.result_denominator: 3 seeds: with prior 80.0-91.7%, without prior 36.7-70.0% after 12 h.
claims.allowed_conclusion: A good prior from the LLM trajectory speeds per-task model learning in three simulated tasks; no transfer or retention claim.

assessment.evidence_level_reason: Closed-loop success on a real arm with per-task counts and a 13-task simulator; prompts were authored per setup and tasks authored by the team, so transfer is not granted.
assessment.strongest_supported_claim: With GPT-4 and a calibrated RGB-D perception pipeline, composing LLM-written 3D value maps for an MPC planner outperforms a primitives-only LLM baseline and a learned-costmap baseline on authored real (5 tasks x 10 trials) and simulated (13 tasks x 20 episodes) manipulation suites, including seen/unseen attributes and disturbances; LLM-trajectory priors speed dynamics learning in three simulated tasks.
assessment.cannot_claim: Open-set generalization beyond authored suites, robustness across LLM backbones, representation-vs-replanning attribution, cost/latency viability, perception robustness.
unresolved: Fairness of the handicapped primitives baseline
